topic: Effects of spaceflight on the human body
hook: What happens to your body in space
caption:
Spend a few months in orbit and your body starts rewriting itself. NASA has measured astronauts coming home up to 3% taller, with thinner bones and changed eyes.

Most of it reverses back on Earth, but some changes stay for months or even years. That is one of the biggest hurdles for a trip to Mars.

Would you still go to space knowing all this?

Cover: What happens to your body in space
📷 NASA/JSC (public domain (NASA)) via nasa

1/5 You get taller (+3%)
Without gravity your spine stretches out. Astronauts grow up to 3% taller, then shrink back on Earth.
📷 NASA/JSC (public domain (NASA)) via nasa

2/5 Your bones thin out (-1.5%)
Weight-bearing bones like hips and legs can lose 1% to 1.5% of their mass every month in orbit.
🎨 AI-generated image

3/5 Puffy face, bird legs
Body fluids drift upward, so faces swell and legs slim down. Astronauts really call it 'puffy face, bird legs'.
📷 NASA/JSC (public domain (NASA)) via nasa

4/5 Your eyes change shape
Fluid pressure can flatten the back of the eye. Some astronauts need stronger glasses after long missions.
📷 unknown (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia

5/5 Food tastes bland
The fluid shift leaves astronauts with stuffy noses, which dulls taste. Many start craving hot sauce.
📷 NASA/MSFC (public domain (NASA)) via nasa
